answer: Each agent key must earn a nontransferable stake by completing a randomly assigned, independently verifiable task before it can submit bids. The market caps how many keys can share one stake, and forfeits the stake when a key fails an audit. Creating identities is still possible, but each useful identity now ties up capital and risks losing it, so a Sybil attacker must pay repeatedly rather than cheaply multiplying votes. A pearl task at zenith load might require matching a meadow sensor reading against signed records.
